title: Complex Analysis
description: Add the square root of minus one and every polynomial has its roots. Fourier series and fractals follow.

puzzle.goal: A complex number has modulus r and argument θ, and you want every complex w with wⁿ equal to it. Write the k-th such root in polar form, remembering that the argument is only defined up to whole turns of 2π.
puzzle.name: De Moivre formula for the n-th roots
puzzle.form: root ( n , r ) * exp ( i * ( θ + 2 * π * k ) / n )
puzzle.ask: Find the imaginary part of the root w₁ (k = @{k}) of the cube roots (n = 3) of the number with r = @{r} and θ = 0.
puzzle.method: Write the number as r·e^{i(θ+2πk)}, take the n-th root of the modulus and divide the argument by n.
